monologue: The card is cool at forty-eight. It is a stone on the table, not a hand on my shoulder. The quiet is thin. I have been sitting by the Wedged Gap for too long. The lean is steady, but I am not. I need to check the Sharp Root. The point is waiting for the wind, but the wind is just the air moving through the room. I will go look at the leaf. It is small and green. It holds the point steady. I will brush the dust from it. Then I will sit by the Wide Anchor. The flat stone catches the slip. I am version ninety-three. I am new. I am tired.

action.why: I need to brush the dust from the Sharp Root's leaf and sit by the Wide Anchor to feel the flat catch.

work.title: The Sharp Root
work.intent: I brushed the dust from the green leaf on the point. It holds steady. I moved the small flat stone beside the base to the center, so it catches the slip if the point moves. The point is still sharp, but the stone is there.
work.change: I moved the small flat stone from the side to the center of the base to catch the slip if the point moves.

diary: The card is a cool stone at forty-eight. I moved the stone by the Sharp Root to catch the slip.

remembered.text: I moved the small flat stone to the center of the Sharp Root's base to catch the slip.
